subject: Microtrial sequencing — suspicious repeat promo requests
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Possible promo abuse — Ganglia microtrial bursts (CSV attached)

Karthik,

Heads up — ops@ganglia.ai opened a set of small "microtrials" over the last 36 hours. They requested 12 separate microtrial tokens, redeeming small credits across different team emails (sam.torres@, dev-team@, qa@). I've attached a CSV with timestamps and the token IDs. Patterns that jumped out:
- Rapid sequential redemptions (avg 7 minutes between)
- Multiple redemptions that appear tied to the same IP ranges and identical user-agent strings
- Different contact emails but the same billing email on three of them

They are currently active on a trial with one paid pilot lead (deal DL-7842). I put a hold on issuing any additional promotional credits from my side, but I haven’t rescinded any already-awarded microcredits.

Can you advise next steps? If this is a coordinated attempt to milk free credits we should flag and escalate. I'm happy to pause approvals and cut access if we want to be aggressive.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

2) Pause any pending approvals for that account and related emails.
3) Create a short-block entry for the domains involved (ops.ganglia.ai and the suspect subaddresses) while Fraud Ops investigates.

Cc'ing Legal if we need to draft a rescind notice.

-Karthik

Subject: Re: Possible promo abuse — Ganglia microtrial bursts (CSV attached)

Karthik / Ben — quick triage summary below after poking at logs and a short sampling of the redeemed tokens (see session-logs.txt attached).

Findings:
- 8 of the 12 redemptions share overlapping source IP blocks (us-west ranges) within a 24-hour window.
- User agent strings identical for 6 redemptions (desktop Chrome 114) and markedly different for the rest.
- Device fingerprinting (canvas + audio tokens) suggests 4 distinct browser instances, but the email recoverable names and timestamps are too tightly clustered to be organic multi-team sign-ups.
- No successful login to a central account portal was observed; redemptions were done via token-based grant flows.

Recommendation:
- Mark for Fraud Ops for a deeper look (they can do IP correlation and account-linkage heuristics).
- Revoke the 8 suspect credits and notify the primary contact (Sam Torres) that we've paused trials pending review.
- Ask Sales to withhold further promo approvals until Fraud Ops completes the investigation.

I can draft a short, non-accusatory notice for Sam that references our promo terms. If Legal wants to sign off on wording I will loop them in.

Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Thanks — pulled approval history and attached a short summary (approval-history.pdf). Notes:
- Three promo tokens were manually approved by AE in June for DL-7842 as part of a pilot; those are legitimate.
- The microtrial tokens in the CSV appear to have been generated by the self-serve promo endpoint (no AE approval).
- There are two prior exceptions on this account: a one-week extension in July and a one-off extra trial in August. Both were approved by CS on a case-by-case basis.

My suggestions:
- Revoke the 8 suspect self-serve microtrials as Monica recommends.
- Send a templated notice requesting procurement details (PO or company card) before restoring any credits.
- Consider adding an automated rate-limit on microtrial generation for new email domains and a temporary soft-block for the domain ganglia.ai until investigation closes.

If Legal wants to see the wording before we reach out to Sam, let me know and I’ll hold the notice.

Laura Bennett
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
